title: Booktabs tables taller than about 90pt between rules keep only the header row; the table body becomes paragraph sentences
evidence:
Code: find_tables (ingest.py:779-788) links two horizontal rules only when `bot - top <= 90` and no strong barrier lies between them. The table box is the rule skeleton plus the rows inside it (lines 820-829). With \toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule, a body taller than 90pt therefore never links midrule to bottomrule, and the region ends at the midrule.

Synthetic repro (L1/scripts/booktabs.py; L1 = <scratch>): a plain numeric booktabs table with a 12pt row pitch.
- 5, 6 or 7 body rows: tab1 bbox [119.5,93,475.5,176/188/200], which is correct.
- 8, 10 or 15 rows: tab1 bbox [119.5,93,475.5,112], header only.
- With 8 rows (L1/edge/out/booktabs8/doc.json): the body becomes p2.b3 type paragraph '…' with sentence p2.s2, plus three '…' blocks of numbers.

Real papers:
- draft C: 8 of 10 tables (tab1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10) have bbox height 20pt, i.e. the header strip only. Every body cell is a paragraph block with sentences (L1/draftC/_debug/page-03.png, page-05.png; one-word sentences such as p3.s3 '…' and p5.s4 '…').
- draft A: tab2 p4 bbox [70,289.5,306.11,311] is the header only. The body is p4.b17 paragraph '…' with sentences p4.s10-s12 (L1/testpaper/_debug/page-04.png).
suggested_fix: Do not cap the rule link at 90pt. Link consecutive full-width rules of near-equal x-extent, stopping at a caption, a heading or a multi-line paragraph of normal body text. When a rule skeleton is found, also absorb the multi-cell rows between the caption side and the last rule. A regression test with an 8+ row booktabs table would have caught this.
verifier: I re-ran L1'…'Model-1 Model-2 ...'…'other'…'s tables have intermediate rules.

title: On two-column pages, table regions cross the gutter and swallow the other column's table, a neighbouring figure, and stray text
evidence:
Code has two causes:
1. find_tables 'beside' (ingest.py:826-827) adds any non-strong row within `expand(skeleton, 40, 0)`. That is 40pt horizontally, with no column restriction, while the ACM gutter is about 24pt.
2. Rule linking (783-786) joins horizontal rules up to 90pt apart that overlap by 50% of the shorter rule, so a short figure line under a table joins it.

SkinnerDBpaper.pdf, page 13 (gutter 306.5, cols L 54-294, R 318-558):
- The Table 6 skeleton is [319,263,557,416]. It absorbed the Figure 6 legend-box lines (372,406,389,406) and (372,416,389,416), shown by L1/scripts/tabdbg.py.
- 'Beside' then grew it to tab6 [170.82,262,557,426.75], deep into the left column.
- tab4 grew to [61,315.87,359.47,426.5], into the right column.
- ingest warns 'page 13: no graphics found for Figure 6', so fig6 is missing.
- Table 4's numeric columns and Figure 6's axis labels are typed as tab6 table_text (p13.b25-b36: 'Total Time Max. Time none 2,268 332', 'Speedup', 'Run Time (%)').
- Figure 6's two side-by-side sub-captions become one paragraph sentence, p13.s18: '(a) MonetDB spends most time (b) SkinnerDB realizes high speedup executing a few expensive queries.'
- The crop L1/skinner/figures/tab6.png shows half of Table 4, part of its caption and the Figure 6 plots.

Skinner page 12: tab1 and tab2 start at x0=286.71 while their rule skeletons start at x0=317. L1/skinner/figures/tab1.png contains left-column text fragments and the proof QED box.
suggested_fix: Clamp the 'beside' expansion to the caption's column span (page.cols[cap.cls]) and never across page.gutter. Link rules only when their widths are comparable (for example a width ratio of at least 0.6). Do not link rules that sit inside another caption's figure band.
verifier: I re-ingested SkinnerDBpaper.pdf and ran a skeleton dump from a scratch copy of the code. On page 13 the gutter is 306.5. The Table 6 skeleton [319,263,557,416] includes the Figure 6 legend lines (372,406,389,406) and (372,416,389,416), which are about 17pt wide but linked through the 50%-of-shorter-rule test. The 'beside' rule (expand(skeleton,40,0), with no column limit) then grows the final bbox to [170.8,262,557,426.7]. tab4 becomes [61,315.9,359.5,426.5], 'no graphics found for Figure 6' is printed, and p13.s18 merges both sub-captions. The tab6.png crop clearly shows half of Table 4 plus the Figure 6 plots. On page 12, tab1.png includes the ends of left-column lines and the QED box. Two-column papers with tables next to the gutter are common.

title: IEEE-style roman-numeral section headings (I., II., III.) are never detected, and outline matching cannot rescue them
evidence:
Code:
- NUM_HEADING_RE (ingest.py:40) only accepts digits.
- is_heading_like (707-716) needs bold or a font at least 1.1x body size, and IEEEtran headings are regular-weight small caps at body size.
- In build_sections, matches() (1317-1319) uses LETTER_HEADING_RE (41), which allows a single letter only. 'II. RELATED WORK' therefore never matches the outline title 'Related Work'.
- classify (1205-1215) types everything between the title and the first detected heading on page 1 as 'authors', so 'I. INTRODUCTION' is excluded from the outline candidates.

Synthetic IEEE-like paper (L1/scripts/ieee2.py; small-caps headings, 10/8pt, regular weight):
- Without an outline (L1/edge/out/ieee2_notoc): 0 sections. 'II. RELATED WORK' is a paragraph split into sentences 'II.' and 'RELATED WORK'. 'I. INTRODUCTION' is typed authors. REFERENCES is a paragraph, so references are not split.
- With a PDF outline (ieee2_toc): warnings for 'Introduction', 'Related Work', 'Method' and 'Experiments' ('has no matching heading'). Only 'V. CONCLUSION' (a single-letter numeral) and REFERENCES become sections.
suggested_fix: Accept roman numerals in the heading regexes (^(?:[IVX]{1,5})\.\s+). Treat centred all-caps or small-caps single lines at body size as heading candidates. Strip a numeral prefix before outline matching. Do not let the 'authors' range swallow a block that matches a numbered heading or outline entry.
verifier: I built a real IEEEtran conference paper with pdflatex and hyperref (outline included). 'II. RELATED WORK', 'III. METHOD' and 'IV. EXPERIMENTS' are paragraphs, split into the sentences 'II.' / 'RELATED WORK' and so on. The outline cannot rescue them: ingest warns that 'Related Work', 'Method' and 'Experiments' have no matching heading. Only 'I. INTRODUCTION' and 'V. CONCLUSION' (single letters, which LETTER_HEADING_RE accepts) and REFERENCES become sections. Subsections 'A. Overview' and 'B. Training' become level-1 sections. One detail differs from the synthetic repro: in the real build, I. INTRODUCTION was detected rather than typed 'authors'. Beyond the finding, the same build also lost the IEEE table entirely: the 'TABLE I' caption has no colon or period, so CAPTION_RE does not match. IEEE is a mainstream format, so I raise this to high.

title: Figures above the median 'first body line' or below the median 'last body line' are discarded; one-page and short PDFs lose top-of-page figures
evidence:
Code: find_figures (ingest.py:884-886) keeps only clusters with `bbox[3] >= top-2 and bbox[1] <= bottom+2`, where (top, bottom) = estimate_text_area (1719-1730). That is the median over pages of each page's first and last full-width body-size row. A page that starts with a figure pushes the median down.

Attention paper:
- Page 4 alone as a one-page PDF (L1/edge/only4.pdf): '…', 0 figures.
- Pages 1-5 (L1/edge/control5.pdf): Figure 2 is lost. text_area is (274.39, 723.18) against (74.41, 722.41) for the full paper, and the Figure 2 images end at y=267.3.
- Pages 13-15 (L1/edge/att_13to15.pdf): Figures 3 and 5 are lost.

Single-page extracts of every figure page of the five PDFs (L1/edge/single/*.pdf): 14 of 35 figures report '…':
- Attention: all 5.
- paper B: figures 1, 2, 3 and 7.
- draft A: figures 7, 8 and 10.
- Skinner: figures 4 and 7.

Root cause re-verified on several of these: cn_p03 text_area top 293 against fig1 cluster bottom 280; em_p10 top 247.5 against fig8 bottom 237; sk_p14 top 220 against cluster bottoms 144-150.

Bottom side: L1/edge/dotgrid.pdf, a one-page PDF with a figure below the last full-width paragraph, also loses its figure.
suggested_fix: Do not filter figure clusters by a document-wide median type area. Use it only to drop thin or short clusters (running-head rules, logos) that lie above the page's own topmost text row or below its bottom-most row. Alternatively use a fixed page margin (for example 4% of the height).
verifier: I made my own extracts of the demo paper. Page 4 alone, pages 1-5, 1-4 and 13-15 each print '…' (Figure 2; Figures 3 and 5). A scratch copy that prints stats.text_area gives (274.4,723.2) for pages 1-5 and (602.3,634.2) for pages 13-15, against (74.4,722.4) for the full paper. Forcing text_area to (0,10000) brings every lost figure back, so the filter at lines 884-886 is the cause. I rate it medium, not high: on all five full real papers and on a 6-page LaTeX article with top-of-page figures, no figure was lost this way. A real 2-page LaTeX paper with a top figure also kept it. It fails on short or float-heavy documents, where most pages start with a figure.

title: Two-column page whose one column is mostly a figure or table is treated as single-column: that column's figures and tables are dropped and text merges across columns
evidence:
Code:
- detect_gutter (ingest.py:388-395) needs at least 20% of the wide rows on each side.
- When it returns None, column_bounds (434-436) sets cols F to the most common row start/end, which is the text-heavy column only.
- find_figures then requires x_overlap with that span (891, 904), so graphics in the other column are never candidates.
- order_page and split_references treat the page as one column.

draft A, page 8: the gutter is None (L1/scripts/gut.py shows left 36 and right 7 of 43 candidate rows).
- '…', so Table 4 is missing.
- The table rows are merged into left-column reference entries, for example p8.b16: '…'.
- p8.b25 ends '…'.
- The Table 4 caption is assigned to sec-references.

Synthetic repro (L1/scripts/twocol.py → L1/edge/twocol_figcol.pdf): a full left column, and a right column holding a 445pt figure, a 2-line caption and 4 text lines. Result: '…', 0 figures, and gutter None for that page.
suggested_fix: When the gutter is None, set cols F to (min x0, max x1) of the body rows instead of the mode. Detect the gutter from a vertical whitespace band that is free of both text and graphics. Alternatively, lower the 20% rule when the minority side contains a caption or graphics.
verifier: In the re-ingested draft A output, page 8 has gutter None and cols F=L=R=(71,289), the left column only. The warning '…' appears. Reference blocks span both columns: p8.b16 [12,213,590,245] and p8.b25 [12,251,587,361]. The Table 4 caption is in sec-references, and the Table 5 caption is under sec-b while its rows are under sec-f. L1'…'no graphics found for Figure 1'…'s second line became a separate block that acts as a strong barrier. Either way it comes from the page being treated as one column, as claimed.

title: Pages with /Rotate 90/270 get bboxes in unrotated space but page width/height in rotated space, and the figure crop is wrong
evidence:
Setup: L1/edge/rotated_p3.pdf is Attention pages 1-5 with page 3 set to /Rotate 90.
- doc.json gives page 3 as {width 792, height 612}, the rotated size.
- Every text bbox is identical to the unrotated control, for example caption p3.b1 [210.01,404.75,401.99,414.71] and p3.b7 [107.64,701.54,505.25,722.4] with y > 612.
- validate.py: 'OK, 0 errors, 16 warnings ... extends past the page (792 x 612)'.
- rotated_all_skinner.pdf gives 106 such warnings.
- ingest itself exits 0 with no warning.

The player reads page sizes from pdf.js with rotation applied (player/src/pdf.ts:11-16, getViewport), so every highlight on such a page is misplaced.

The fig1 crop (L1/edge/out/rotated_p3/figures/fig1.png) shows body text and the caption instead of the Transformer diagram. The fig1 bbox [195.56,107,416.44,395.42] differs from the unrotated [196.5,72.5,415.5,394].

Rotated pages are produced by pdflscape and lscape for landscape appendix tables.
suggested_fix: Transform every extracted rect (text, drawings, images) with page.rotation_matrix into the rotated (displayed) space before analysis, and build crops with the same convention. At minimum, warn and normalise rotated pages.
verifier: I set page 3 of a 5-page demo extract to /Rotate 90. doc.json then reports the page as 792x612, while the bboxes match the unrotated page (p3.b7 y up to 722.4). ingest exits 0 with no warning, and validate.py reports 16 'extends past the page' warnings. ingest.py has no rotation handling (no hits for rotation or rotation_matrix), and player pdf.ts uses getViewport with rotation applied. I also built a real pdflatex + pdflscape landscape table page, and the result is worse than the finding describes: every line on that page is vertical text typed 'other', and Table 2 is never detected. I rate it medium because landscape pages are uncommon and mostly in appendices.

title: A body-text line that starts with "Figure N." or "Table N." is taken as a caption: it splits the paragraph, gets typed as a caption, and can steal the figure from the real caption
evidence: CAPTION_RE (ingest.py:39) is tested against any row in starts_new_block (482-484), any block in mark_barriers (739-744) and classify_block (1139-1140), with no typographic check (gap, bold label, size, whether the previous line ended a sentence). find_figures (870, 889-943) takes captions in y order, and the first caption to claim a graphic keeps it. Repro (scratch .../review/L2/capline/mk3.py -> steal.pdf): a paragraph with the line '...The training curves are in' / 'Figure 1. We then study ...', then the graphic, then the real caption 'Figure 1: Training curves of both models.' ingest.py prints 'warning: page 1: no graphics found for 'Figure 1: Training curves of both models''. In outline.py: fig1 has caption p1.b2 'Figure 1. We then study which parts of the model matter most ...' (body text), so the real caption is orphaned and is even listed as fig1.referenced_by = p1.s5. The sentence is cut as p1.s3 'The training curves are in' and p1.s4 'Figure 1. We then study ...'. Even without the theft (capline2.pdf/out2), the rest of the paragraph becomes block p1.b2 of type 'caption', the sentence is split the same way, and a spurious warning appears. Control (mk_ctrl.py, the same text with the reference mid-line) gives one paragraph, no warning, and the correct caption. A sentence-final reference wrapped to the start of a line is common in papers. The demo is not affected (its line-initial 'Table 2 summarizes' has no punctuation after the number).
suggested_fix: Accept a caption candidate only when it starts a visually separate block: the previous row in the column ends a sentence, or there is a vertical gap above leading, or the label word is bold or differs from body size. When several candidates share a (kind, number), let the one with the caption signature (bold label, smaller size, ':' after the number) or the one nearest the graphic claim the region, and never let a candidate that continues a paragraph claim graphics or table skeletons. find_tables (766, 800-818) uses the same first-come claiming and needs the same guard.
verifier: I rebuilt steal.pdf from L2's mk3.py in verify-L2/cap and ran ingest.py on it. It printed "warning: page 1: no graphics found for 'Figure 1: Training curves of both models'". outline.py shows fig1's caption as p1.b2 "Figure 1. We then study ..." (body text), the paragraph cut into p1.s3 "The training curves are in" and p1.s4 "Figure 1. We then ...", and the real caption orphaned as p1.b3. L2's own control used a different layout, so I built one with the same layout as steal.pdf (mkc.py -> ctrl.pdf), changing only where the line breaks around "Figure 1.". It gives one paragraph, no warning, and fig1.caption_block set to the real caption. Code confirms the cause. starts_new_block (ingest.py:482-484) and mark_barriers (739-744) test CAPTION_RE (line 39) on any line, with no check of gap, font or whether the previous line ended a sentence. find_figures takes captions in y order and a caption keeps the graphic once it has claimed it. This is not among the build report's known limitations. It is a real bug, but it needs a sentence-final reference to wrap to the start of a line, followed by '.' or ':'. The demo is unaffected, so medium.

title: A whitespace-only `say` passes validate.py, but the player then rejects the whole tour
evidence: The schema only has minLength 1 on say, and validate.py never checks that say has words (line 289 computes n_words=0 and moves on). Variant .../review/L2/variants/blank_say/attention (one step with say " ") gives 'validate ...: OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings'. The player's checkTour (validate.ts:75, `!st.say.trim()`) returns 'chapters[0].steps[0].say must be a non-empty string' (shown by running the real code: node .../L2/player_check.cjs variants/blank_say/attention). load.ts:66-68 then sets tour = null, so not one step of the tour plays, although the guardrail said OK. README 'Next 1' presents validate.py as the guardrail for LLM-written tours.
suggested_fix: In validate.py, report an error when `not step['say'].split()` ("say has no words"), or add `"pattern": "\\S"` to the say schema. Better still, have the player drop or skip only the bad step, with a problem entry, instead of refusing the whole tour.
verifier: blank_say/tour.json has say " ". validate.py prints 'OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings', because the schema only has minLength 1 and validate.py:289 just computes n_words=0. I bundled the real player/src/validate.ts with esbuild in my own script (verify-L2/js/pc.ts). checkTour returns ["chapters[0].steps[0].say must be a non-empty string"] (validate.ts:75, !st.say.trim()). load.ts:66-68 then leaves tour as null, so the whole tour is refused. README line 92 calls validate.py the guardrail. The input is unusual, and the player's error names the exact field, which lowers the impact. Still, the guardrail and the player disagree, and the result is zero playable steps. That makes it a real bug in a less common path: medium.

title: A focus action on a page the loaded PDF does not have throws inside App's camera effect and blanks the whole app
evidence:
Test: sh <scratch> focus_nopage.test.ts. It uses the real demo doc.json and tour.json and does what App does: layoutPages(sizes), new Resolver(doc, sizes), prepareTour, the engine, then cameraView for each step.

Case 1, PDF failed to open (sizes = []): prepareTour reports 0 problems. 17 of the 38 steps throw "step 0 (welcome) focus \"p1.b2\": Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')".

Case 2, doc.json from a longer PDF (the PDF has 3 pages): 11 steps throw, starting at "step 13 (equation-1) focus \"eq1\"".

Why:
- camera.ts:87 calls focusView(target.rect, layout.pages[target.page - 1], ...) and that page is undefined.
- toStage (layout.ts) quietly returns the unshifted rect when the page is missing.
- Resolver.resolve and prepareTour (resolve.ts:109-137, 152-157) never check a sentence, block or figure page against pageSizes. Only pageN IDs are checked.
- load.ts:79-86 records a PDF failure as a problem but still returns the doc and tour, so Play stays enabled.
- App.tsx:143-145 calls frame() in a useEffect with no try/catch, and main.tsx has no error boundary. React 18 therefore unmounts the whole tree on Play, which also removes the banner that explains the PDF error.

A realistic trigger is ingest.py --out. ingest.py:1892-1893 writes source.file as a path relative to the original PDF and does not copy the PDF. Reproduced: ingest.py demo/attention/paper.pdf --out <scratch>/ingest_out/attention2 produced source.file "../../../../../../../../../..<local path>". load.ts:81 builds the PDF URL from that path, and the dev server cannot serve it.
suggested_fix: Resolver: treat any ID whose page is greater than pageSizes.length (or any ID at all when no PDF is loaded) as unknown, so prepareTour drops it with a warning. In cameraView, return null when layout.pages[target.page - 1] is missing. Wrap frame() in try/catch and add a top-level error boundary. Consider disabling Play when the PDF failed to load.
verifier: I re-ran `sh .../review/L3/run.sh focus_nopage.test.ts`. With sizes=[], prepareTour reports 0 problems and 17 steps throw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')", starting with step 0 (welcome) focus p1.b2. With a 3-page PDF, 11 steps throw, starting at step 13 (eq1). The code matches the report. camera.ts:87 passes layout.pages[target.page-1], which is undefined here, into focusView, and readingScale(page.width) throws. layout.ts toStage returns the rect unchanged when the page is missing. Resolver.resolve and kind() only check pageN IDs against pageSizes. load.ts:82-86 adds the PDF failure as a problem but still returns doc and tour. ControlBar disables Play only when there are no steps. App.tsx:143-145 calls frame() in a useEffect with no try/catch, and a grep of src finds no error boundary. In React 18.3.1 an uncaught error in an effect unmounts the root, so the banner disappears too. The first Play throws right away because step 0's focus fires at word 0. Next, Prev and sidebar jumps hit the same path through showStep/rebuild. I also confirmed the --out trigger: the L3 scratch doc.json has source.file '../../../../../../../../../..<local path>'. When --out is under demo/ and the PDF is outside it, the browser normalizes the URL to a path outside publicDir. That fetch most likely gets the SPA's index.html and fails to open; I inferred this and did not request the URL. The build report mentions the relative source.file but not this crash. The crash needs doc.json and tour.json present with the PDF unreachable, which is a less common error path, but it turns a readable error banner into a blank app. Medium.

title: Without voices or a working speech backend, every step waits 1.5–5.5 s before any narration progress, and this repeats on every step
evidence:
Test: sh <scratch> speech_dead.test.ts. It runs the real createNarrator, WebSpeechNarrator and TourEngine with a fake clock and a fake speechSynthesis.

(a) getVoices() is [] and speak() never starts. Delay to the first word per step: [5502,5502,5502] ms. The 3-step tour takes 28400 ms, against 11900 ms for the same tour muted. That is three speak() calls and three '[speech] falling back' warnings: the cost is paid again on every step.

(b) Speech works but getVoices() stays []. Delay from step start to speak(): [1501,1501,1501] ms on every step.

Causes:
- webSpeech.ts:64-74: loadVoices sets voicesPromise = null when the list is empty, so every step waits the 1500 ms timeout again.
- webSpeech.ts:186-188: the 4000 ms START_TIMEOUT watchdog runs per utterance.
- webSpeech.ts:139-145: the fallback applies only to the current step. Nothing marks speech as broken.
- index.ts:25 picks speech whenever the API exists.

For the 38-step demo this adds about 209 s of dead air in case (a) and about 57 s in case (b). Plausible environments are browsers that expose speechSynthesis with no voices or TTS backend, such as Chromium on Linux without speech-dispatcher, VMs and kiosks. That real-browser behaviour was not verified here; the test models it with a fake synth.
suggested_fix: Remember a failed or empty voice load: wait for voices once, then use whatever getVoices() returns. After a 'speech did not start' (or not-allowed / synthesis-unavailable) fallback, mark speech unavailable for the session so the router uses the silent narrator at once. Optionally show an info problem such as 'Speech unavailable, using timed narration'.
verifier: I re-ran speech_dead.test.ts and got the same numbers: the first word comes [5502,5502,5502] ms into each step, the 3-step tour takes 28400 ms against 11900 ms muted, with 3 speak() calls and 3 fallback warnings. In case (b), speak() starts [1501,1501,1501] ms after each step begins. The code confirms the cause. webSpeech.ts:69 resets voicesPromise to null when the voice list is empty, so the 1500 ms wait comes back every step. The 4000 ms START_TIMEOUT watchdog (line 187) is set for each utterance. fallback() (139-145) only covers the current speak() call and nothing records that speech failed. createNarrator (index.ts:25) picks WebSpeech whenever the API exists. The build report treats the 4 s fallback as a fix ('falls back ... after 4 s instead of up to about 40 s') and does not list the per-step repeat as a limitation. Whether real browsers expose speechSynthesis with no voices and a speak() that never starts, as Linux Chromium without speech-dispatcher might, is unverified. A typical Mac or Windows demo setup will not hit it, and the user can work around it with Mute. When it does happen, every step gets 1.5-5.5 s of dead air. That is a real defect on a less common path: medium.

title: During a continuous wheel or trackpad scroll, every page passed is kept at full resolution (all 15 pages, about 465 MB of canvas)
evidence:
Stage.tsx:143-148 calls planScales(..., keep = moving). Each wheel event goes through Camera.userInput (camera.ts:180-189), which sends notify(true) and restarts the 160 ms settle timer (SETTLE_MS, camera.ts:32). During a momentum scroll the events arrive about every 16 ms, so `moving`, and with it `keep`, stays true for the whole gesture. planScales line 57 (`if (keep) return Math.max(cur, target)`) then never releases or downgrades a page, so each page that scrolls into view gets a visible-scale canvas (preview pass plus full pass) and keeps it until the gesture ends.
Test setup: headless Chromium 148 against `vite preview` of the existing player/dist, 1440x900 at DPR 2, synthetic 60 Hz WheelEvents with deltaY 120 for 3.2 s (script <scratch>, run twice).
Result: at idle there are 2 canvases (12.1 MP). At the peak there are 116.3 MP (all 15 pages at 4 px/pt, about 465 MB of backing store), with 36 pdf.js render passes. In t4.mjs, at the end of the fling pages 1-13 held full-resolution canvases while the visible pages 14 and 15 had none yet.
Comparison: I built a one-line variant in scratch (mod/player) that passes `moving && camera.targetView !== view` instead of `moving`, so keep applies only while the camera animates. Under the same fling its peak is 19.9 MP, with the same blank-visible time, and tour camera flights are unchanged.
suggested_fix: Apply `keep` only while the camera is animating, not during user input. In Stage.tsx apply(), call planScales(layout, planView, camera.viewport.height, prev.scales, moving && camera.targetView !== view), or expose a Camera.animating getter. Pages that leave the near band during a manual scroll are then released, and their in-flight renders are cancelled by the existing effect cleanup.
verifier: The code path is clear. Stage.tsx:148 passes `moving` as `keep`. Camera.userInput (camera.ts:180-189) sends notify(true) and restarts the 160 ms settle timer on every wheel event. During user input there is no animation, so targetView === view, and planScales line 57 (`Math.max(cur, target)`) never releases a page. I reproduced it with my own script (verify-L4/v1.mjs: headless Chromium 148 against a fresh `vite preview` of player/dist, which is newer than src; 1440x900 at DPR 2; JS WheelEvents with deltaY 120 every 16 ms for 3.2 s). At idle: 12.1 MP, scales [4,3,0,...]. While the gesture runs, every page that has been passed keeps 4 px/pt: [4,4,4,4,4,4,1,0..] at about 1 s, and all 15 pages at 4 px/pt at the end, 116.3 MP (about 465 MB of backing store). 1.5 s after the gesture ends, 15.5 MP remain (only pages 14 and 15). So the build is transient, but it is real: it grows with paper length, and a 40-page paper would pass 1 GB during a long fling. The build report does not list it; its canvas cap note is about each canvas, not the total. It also goes against the planner comment that rendering should follow where the camera is going. The suggested fix (apply keep only while animating) matches the intent of the code.

title: Touch devices cannot pan or zoom the paper: the stage sets touch-action:none but only handles wheel events
evidence:
styles.css:219 sets `.viewport { touch-action: none; }`, which disables native touch panning and pinch on the stage. Stage.tsx:176-196 registers only a 'wheel' listener, and a grep of player/src for touch, pointer and gesture handlers finds none (the 375px layout was explicitly 'checked and fixed').
Test: headless Chromium at 390x780, mobile, DPR 3, touch emulation on (t6.mjs). A one-finger drag of 300 px and a two-finger pinch-out both leave the stage at `translate(-2.71895px, 0px) scale(0.584967)`, the same as before. At that scale 10 pt body text is about 5.9 CSS px.
Impact: the user cannot scroll past page 1 or zoom in. Only the tour camera moves the view, and with no tour.json nothing does. Desktop mice without a wheel also have no drag-to-pan.
suggested_fix: Add pointer handlers on the viewport. One pointer drag calls camera.panBy(-dx, -dy) (also useful with the mouse). Two pointers call camera.zoomAt(dist/prevDist, midX, midY) plus a pan by the midpoint delta. Keep touch-action:none so the browser does not compete. Use setPointerCapture, and ignore clicks after a drag so the D-overlay click-to-copy still works.
verifier: styles.css:219 sets `.viewport { touch-action: none; }`. Stage.tsx registers only a 'wheel' listener, and a grep of player/src finds no touch, pointer or gesture handlers. I reproduced it with my own script (verify-L4/v3.mjs: 390x780, mobile, DPR 3, touch emulation on, CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent). The page received the touch events (touchstart 3, touchmove 39, pointermove 60). The stage transform stayed `translate(-2.71895px, 0px) scale(0.584967)` after a 300 px one-finger drag and after a two-finger pinch-out, and visualViewport.scale stayed 1. The sidebar is display:none below 860px, so on a phone the tour transport is the only way to move. The tour still plays and moves the camera, so the demo is not broken on phones, but free reading and zooming are impossible there. The report says mobile layout was 'checked and fixed' but does not list this limitation.

title: An explicit note side is honoured even when there is no room on that side, so at phone width the card covers its anchor
evidence:
chooseSide (ScreenLayer.tsx:51-52) returns `pref` whenever it is not 'auto'. placeCard then clamps the card back into the viewport, on top of the anchor.
Test (notes.sh, which simulates the tour's 7 notes with the player's own modules and computes the room on the requested side for a card of min(300px, 70% of width)): at 1152x720 and 1112x767 every explicit side fits. At 992x620, step 17 (mh-numbers, side right) is 8 px short. At 375x560, 5 of the 6 explicit-side notes have no room, and the card overlaps its anchor by 99-250 px (steps 5, 6, 12, 17, 25). The tour author set explicit sides for 6 of 7 notes after tuning at 1152x720.
suggested_fix: Treat an explicit side as a preference. If room[pref] < need[pref], fall back to the automatic choice (or the opposite side when that fits).
verifier: chooseSide (ScreenLayer.tsx:52) returns `pref` whenever it is not 'auto'. placeCard then clamps the card back into the viewport, on top of the anchor. I measured the real DOM with my own script (verify-L4/v7.mjs), computing each note anchor from the doc.json bbox plus its region and comparing it with the .note card rect at paused steps 6, 7, 13, 16, 18, 26 and 31. At 1440x900 (stage 1152x806) and 1280x720 there is no overlap. At 1280x800 (stage 992x706), the step 18 card covers 25% of its anchor and step 7 covers 5%. At a 1100x760 window (stage 812x666), the step 6 and step 18 cards cover their anchors completely, step 7 covers 54% and step 13 covers 10%. At 390x844 mobile, all 5 explicit left/right notes (steps 6, 7, 13, 18, 26) cover 100% of their anchors. So the problem shows up at moderately narrow desktop windows as well as on phones, which is why I rate it medium rather than low. The build report's note-side limitation is about auto placement, and the author tuned the explicit sides at an assumed 1152x720 stage; the missing fallback for explicit sides is not listed. One caveat: falling back to auto may not always do better, because the report says auto often covers the subject in zoomed figures.

title: Quick start fails on macOS's built-in python3 (3.9) because the pinned pymupdf needs Python 3.10 or later, and the README lists no prerequisites
evidence: /usr/bin/python3 --version -> Python 3.9.6 (stock macOS). Ran the README's step 1 with it: '/usr/bin/python3 -m venv py39' worked. Step 2, 'py39/bin/pip install -r ingest/requirements.txt', failed with: 'ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement pymupdf==1.27.2.3 (from versions: ... 1.26.4, 1.26.5) / No matching distribution found'. The installed pymupdf-1.27.2.3.dist-info/METADATA says 'Requires-Python: >=3.10'. The vite package.json says 'node: ^18.0.0 || >=20.0.0'. README.md (lines 29-37) names no Python or Node version, and player/package.json has no 'engines' field. The same steps passed with miniconda Python 3.13.5 and Node 25.8.1. Scratch venv: <scratch>
suggested_fix: Add a Prerequisites line to the README: Python 3.10+ and Node 18+ (for example `python3.12 -m venv ingest/.venv`). Optionally add "engines": {"node": ">=18"} to player/package.json. Also note that the player alone does not need Python, because the demo's doc.json is committed.
verifier: Reproduced. /usr/bin/python3 is 3.9.6. In a fresh 3.9 venv in scratch (verify-L6/py39v), `pip download pymupdf==1.27.2.3` fails with 'No matching distribution found'; the newest version it lists is 1.26.5. The installed pymupdf-1.27.2.3 METADATA says 'Requires-Python: >=3.10'. The three ingest scripts parse under 3.9, so only the version pin rules it out. Mitigating: on this machine python3 resolves to miniconda 3.13 first, the error is loud rather than silent, and the player runs without Python because the demo doc.json is in the tree. title: Adding a paper with the documented --out flag produces a doc.json the player cannot open, while validate.py still reports OK, and the README has no add-a-paper steps
evidence: In the fresh copy: 'ingest/.venv/bin/python ingest/ingest.py ../papers/transformer.pdf --out demo/transformer' worked, but doc.json source.file = '../../../papers/transformer.pdf'. 'validate.py demo/transformer' -> 'OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings', because it only checks that the file exists on disk. The player builds pdfUrl = `${baseUrl}${doc.source.file}` (load.ts:83), which the browser normalizes to /papers/transformer.pdf. With the dev server running briefly, curl gave 'pdf-normalized 200 text/html' (Vite's index.html fallback), while '/transformer/doc.json' gave 200 application/json. pdf.js therefore gets HTML: the page shows no PDF, only an error banner. The build report mentions the '../../..' path only as a contract note and does not say the player cannot load it. Besides `--out`, the README never says the PDF must live in demo/<name>/, that vite serves only demo/ (publicDir '../demo'), or that you open ?paper=<name>. A folder name that fails /^[\w.-]+$/ (for example one with a space) makes App.tsx readParams silently load 'attention' instead of showing an error.
suggested_fix: Add an 'Add a paper' section: mkdir demo/<name>, copy the PDF to demo/<name>/paper.pdf, run ingest.py on it, write tour.json with "paper": "<name>", run validate.py, then open ?paper=<name>. In ingest.py, when --out differs from the PDF's folder, copy the PDF into --out and set source.file to its basename, or at least have validate.py warn when source.file leaves the paper folder. Have the player report an invalid ?paper= value instead of falling back silently.
verifier: Reproduced in a scratch copy (verify-L6/repo). `ingest.py ../papers/transformer.pdf --out demo/transformer` wrote source.file '../../../papers/transformer.pdf' (ingest.py:1892-1893 uses relpath), and `validate.py demo/transformer` gave 'OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings', because validate.py:134 only checks os.path.isfile(join(folder, file)). load.ts:81 builds pdfUrl = baseUrl + source.file, and new URL() normalizes that to /papers/transformer.pdf. With Vite briefly on port 5199 (publicDir ../demo), curl gave /transformer/doc.json -> 200 application/json, and both /papers/transformer.pdf and the un-normalized path -> 200 text/html (index.html fallback); /attention/paper.pdf -> application/pdf. pdf.js therefore gets HTML. App.tsx:31 silently falls back to 'attention' when ?paper= fails /^[\w.-]+$/. The README never says the PDF must be served from demo/<name>/. The ingest report lists the '../../..' path only as a contract note, not that the player cannot load it, so this goes beyond the known limitation. Mitigating: the player shows an error banner naming the bad URL, and the default flow (PDF inside demo/<name>, no --out) works.

title: Review-mode line numbers are typed as reference entries and glued into references
evidence:
Code: split_references (ingest.py:1379) converts '…' and paragraph blocks under References into references. _split_entries (1394-1399) then takes the line-number column (x=12.2) as the left edge, so every line number starts an entry.
- draft A page 7: p7.b32 '…' and p7.b33 '…' are reference blocks with sentences. p7.b34 is '…'. p7.b37 ends '…'.
- draft A page 8: p8.b1-b3 '…', '…', '…' are separate references.
- Line numbers elsewhere in the body are correctly header_footer.
suggested_fix: Exclude narrow, number-only rows in the outer margins (the same rule that already makes them header_footer elsewhere) before splitting references, and compute x_min from rows that contain letters.
verifier: In the re-ingested draft A output, page 8 blocks p8.b1-b3 ('…', '…', '…') and many more are typed reference. p8.b4 starts '…'. The same margin numbers below the References section (p8.b44-b56) are header_footer. In _split_entries, x_min is the minimum over all rows, which includes the x=12 line-number column, so every line number starts an entry. This only affects review-mode PDFs, so I rate it low.

title: A wrapped bold heading that contains a math glyph is cut at the line break; the second line becomes a paragraph
evidence:
Code: can_join (ingest.py:528) refuses to join when all_bold(prev) != all_bold(row). In the draft A heading '…', the math arrow glyph has bold=0.86 < 0.9.
- Result: section sec-5.2 has the title '…'.
- p4.b34 is a paragraph '…' with its own sentence p4.s26.
- ingest warns '…'.
suggested_fix: In all_bold, ignore non-letter math-font glyphs (or use the bold share of letters only) when deciding whether a row is a bold heading line.
verifier: In the re-ingested draft A output, sec-5.2 is titled '…', and p4.b34 '…' is a separate paragraph with its own sentence p4.s26. The outline warning appears. In the rawdict spans, the arrow is CMSY10 with flags 6 and the rest is NimbusRomNo9L-Medi with flags 20. all_bold (line 496) therefore fails for '…', and can_join (line 528) refuses the join. This is a minor, single-heading defect.

title: Non-PDF files renamed .pdf are accepted (silent success, or a traceback with --debug); encrypted PDFs crash with a traceback
evidence:
Code: main() (ingest.py:1883-1888) accepts anything pymupdf.open can read, which includes HTML, PNG and other formats. It never checks pdf.is_pdf or pdf.needs_pass. doc.json is written (1903-1905) before render_debug runs.

Results:
- L1/edge/html.pdf (an HTML '403 Forbidden' page renamed .pdf), without --debug: exit 0, 'wrote .../doc.json: 1 pages, 1 blocks', and sections [{"id": "sec-403-forbidden"...}].
- The same file with --debug: doc.json is written, then a traceback 'ValueError: is no PDF' at render_debug → p.new_shape() (ingest.py:1833), exit 1.
- notapdf_png.pdf: the same traceback with --debug; exit 0 and an empty doc.json without it.
- encrypted.pdf (user password): a traceback in analyse → read_lines(p) → 'ValueError: document closed or encrypted', exit 1.

For comparison: empty.pdf and a text file fail cleanly ('error: cannot open ... as a PDF'). A truncated PDF fails cleanly but with a misleading message ('error: the PDF has no pages').
suggested_fix: After opening, reject the file unless pdf.is_pdf (or open it with filetype='pdf'). Report pdf.needs_pass and pdf.is_encrypted as a clear 'password-protected PDF' error. Validate before writing anything, and run render_debug inside try/except or before the write.
verifier: I created my own test files. An HTML '403 Forbidden' page saved as .pdf: without --debug, exit 0 and a doc.json titled '403 Forbidden'. With --debug, doc.json is written first and then the run fails with 'ValueError: is no PDF' at render_debug, exit 1. A PNG renamed .pdf behaves the same way, with 0 blocks. An AES-256 PDF with a user password fails with a traceback, 'document closed or encrypted'. main() (lines 1883-1888) never checks is_pdf or needs_pass, and it writes doc.json before render_debug. These are real, but they are error-handling gaps for bad input; valid papers are not affected, so I rate it low.

title: A scanned paper (pages with no text layer) produces an empty doc.json with exit 0 and no message
evidence: L1/edge/scanned.pdf (3 image-only pages) gives 'wrote .../doc.json: 3 pages, 0 blocks, 0 sentences, 0 sections, 0 figures ...', exit 0, empty stderr. mixed_scanned.pdf (one image-only page among text pages) is likewise silent about the empty page. A user gets a paper with nothing to tour and no explanation.
suggested_fix: Warn per page when a page has no text but has a page-sized image ('page N has no text layer; OCR it first'). Exit non-zero with a clear message when the whole document has no text.
verifier: I rendered 4 demo pages to images and wrapped them in a new PDF. ingest exits 0 with empty stderr and prints '4 pages, 0 blocks, 0 sentences ...'. There is no OCR or no-text-layer warning anywhere in ingest.py. The summary line's 0 blocks is the only hint, so I rate it low.

title: Numbered list markers become standalone sentences ('1.', '2.', ...)
evidence:
Code: is_boundary (ingest.py:1484-1500) treats a token ending in '.' followed by a capitalised word as a sentence end, and has no exception for enumerators.
- draft A: p3.s9 '…', p3.s11 '…', p3.s13 '…' are each followed by the item text as a separate sentence.
- draft C: 20+ cases, for example p2.s1 '…', p2.s3 '…' ... p2.s11 '…' in the contributions list, and p13.s1/s3/s5, p14.s7/s10/s13.
- A tour that highlights such a sentence marks only the marker, and outline.py lists '…' as a sentence.
suggested_fix: Do not end a sentence on a token matching ^\(?\d{1,2}[.)]$ (or a single roman numeral or letter enumerator) when it is the first token of a block or row. Alternatively merge it into the following sentence, as is already done for '…' in captions.
verifier: In a real pdflatex article with \enumerate, the markers become the standalone sentences p1.s36 '…', p1.s38 '…' and p1.s40 '…'. is_boundary (lines 1484-1500) has no exception for enumerators, and only captions get the '…' fix. This is a cosmetic or minor targeting issue.

title: The at_word bounds check is skipped for integral floats, and audio word timings are not checked against the word count
evidence: validate.py:300-301 runs the bounds check only when `isinstance(aw, int)`, but the Draft 2020-12 'integer' type accepts 999.0. In variants/float_atword (say 'Look at this figure.', at_word 999.0) validate.py reports OK with 0 errors, while variants/int_atword (999) reports 'at_word: 999 is past the end of `say` (4 words, so 0..3)'. The player Math.floor()s it to 999 and fires the action at the end of the step (prepareTour info: 'at_word 999 ... is past the last word (4 words); it fires at the end.'). Also, variants/audio_times (4 words, word_times_ms [0,300,200], a missing audio file) passes with 0 errors. audio.ts:57 then silently ignores the timings because given.length !== n and falls back to a uniform estimate, so at_word sync degrades without any message.
suggested_fix: Bounds-check any number that is not a bool: `isinstance(aw, (int, float)) and not isinstance(aw, bool)`. When step.audio has word_times_ms, check its length equals len(say.split()) and that it never decreases. Warn when audio.src does not exist.
verifier: I re-ran both variants. float_atword (at_word 999.0) passes validate.py with 0 errors, while int_atword (999) errors. The cause is validate.py:301, which tests isinstance(aw, int), while Draft 2020-12 'integer' accepts 999.0. In the player (my esbuild script), prepareTour gives the info problem 'at_word 999 ... past the last word (4 words); it fires at the end' and schedules at 999. audio_times (word_times_ms of length 3 for a 4-word say, missing src) passes validate.py. audio.ts:57 uses the given timings only when given.length === n, otherwise it silently falls back to a uniform spread. The schema says only 'Start time of each word of say'. Both parts are real. Integral floats are rare, and AudioNarrator is unused (the build report says no tour has audio), so low.

title: validate.py and the player use different whitespace sets to count words, so at_word can point at different words
evidence: validate.py:289 uses Python str.split(). The player (types.ts:215-216 splitWords, which engine, resolve, Sidebar and the WebSpeech chunks all use) uses JS /\s+/. The tour builder (scratch build_tour.py:343) also uses str.split(). Comparing every code point up to U+FFFF: whitespace only in Python is U+001C-U+001F and U+0085; whitespace only in JS is U+FEFF. variants/nel_say ('Look at\u0085this figure.', at_word 3): validate.py counts 4 words and reports OK; the player counts 3 ('atthis') and fires the action at the end. variants/bom_say ('Look at﻿this figure.', at_word 3): validate.py errors '3 is past the end (3 words)', while the player counts 4 words and accepts it. Every index after such a character is shifted by one between the two. All other cases agree: leading and trailing spaces, em dashes, hyphens and numbers are not separators in any of the three. All 38 demo steps (ASCII only) give identical counts in Python and JS, so the demo is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Define words the same way on both sides. Either have validate.py reject say text containing U+001C-U+001F, U+0085 or U+FEFF, or split on one explicit shared class in both languages (for example `[\t\n\v\f\r    -     　﻿]+`, in Python via re.split) and document it in the schema's say description.
verifier: I tested every code point below U+10000. Python str.split() also splits on U+001C-U+001F and U+0085. JS /\s+/ also splits on U+FEFF. The sets are otherwise identical, as claimed. The variants hold the claimed characters ('Look at\x85this figure.' and 'Look at﻿this figure.'). nel_say: validate.py OK (4 words), while the player's splitWords gives 3 words [Look, atthis, figure.] and prepareTour reports at_word 3 fires at the end. bom_say: validate.py errors '3 words', while the player counts 4 and accepts the tour. The mismatch is real, but these characters are very unlikely in narration, and the demo is ASCII, so low.

title: validate.py's 'doc.json is internally consistent' misses several cross-references and the PDF hash
evidence: variants/doc_inconsistent/attention passes with 'OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings', although it contains: sentence p3.s2 (page 3) owned by and listed in block p4.b6 (page 4); fig1 with kind 'table', page 5 and bbox [100,100,200,200] while its caption_block p3.b1 is on page 3; figure_text block p4.b1 owning sentence p4.s99 (the schema says figure_text carries no sentences); eq1.page 4 with eq1.block p7.b12; sentence p2.s1 with its rect moved outside its block. check_doc (164-226) only checks ID-page prefixes, existence and back-links. Also, variants/stale_sha (doc.json source.sha256 does not match paper.pdf, and the tour matches the stale hash) passes: validate.py never hashes the PDF, so a swapped PDF with a stale doc.json goes unnoticed and every coordinate is wrong.
suggested_fix: Add these checks: sentence.page == its block's page; figure.page == caption_block's page; the id prefix (fig/tab) matches kind; equation.block is on equation.page; figure_text/table_text/equation blocks have no sentences; sentence rects lie inside their block bbox (with tolerance). Hash source.file and compare it to source.sha256 (error on mismatch).
verifier: I diffed doc_inconsistent against the demo doc.json, and every claimed defect is present. p3.s2 is moved to block p4.b6. fig1 has kind table, page 5 and bbox [100,100,200,200]. figure_text p4.b1 owns p4.s99. eq1.block is p7.b12. p2.s1's rect is moved out of its block. validate.py still prints 'OK, 0 errors, 0 warnings'. check_doc (lines 164-226) only checks ID page prefixes, existence and back-links. stale_sha: the doc and tour hashes are all zeros while paper.pdf hashes to bdfaa68d..., and validate.py reports OK because it never hashes the PDF. load.ts only compares tour.doc_sha256 with doc.source.sha256, so the player would not notice either. doc.json is machine-generated, so most of these only matter for hand-edited files. A swapped PDF is the one practical case. Low.

title: validate.py crashes with a traceback on some schema-invalid inputs instead of reporting them
evidence: check_tour runs even when the tour fails the schema (338-342), and it assumes valid types. variants/list_step_id (step "id": ["s1"]) fails with 'File ".../validate.py", line 285, in check_tour: if sid in step_ids: TypeError: unhashable type: 'list''. Chapter IDs at line 277 behave the same way. variants/bad_source (doc.json "source": "paper.pdf" plus a tour) fails at line 257: 'AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get''. In both cases none of the collected errors are printed, which defeats the guardrail role for malformed LLM output.
suggested_fix: Use step and chapter IDs as dict keys only when they are strings (otherwise rely on the schema error), and read the hash with `src = doc.get('source'); sha = src.get('sha256') if isinstance(src, dict) else None`. Alternatively, wrap check_tour so that an exception becomes a reported error.
verifier: Both crashes reproduce. With list_step_id ("id": ["s1"]), validate.py fails with TypeError unhashable type: 'list' at validate.py:285. With bad_source (doc.json "source" is a string), it fails with AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get' at line 257. main() calls check_tour after a failed schema check, and the collected errors are never printed because the exception escapes first. Line 277 handles chapter IDs the same way. Other malformed types (say, targets, at_word, speaker) are guarded, so only unhashable IDs and a non-dict source crash, and both are unusual. Low.

title: The sentence splitter never breaks after a single capital letter, so 'Appendix A. We ...' stays one sentence
evidence: is_boundary (ingest.py:1489-1493) lowercases the token before testing `re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]\.", word) and tok.math < 0.5`, so any non-math single letter, upper or lower case, counts as an initial. Feeding the real split_sentences synthetic tokens: 'Proofs are given in Appendix A. We then train the model.' gives one sentence, and 'We call this variant model B. It uses fewer layers.' gives one sentence, while 'Results are in Table 3. No other model comes close.' splits correctly. The demo has no such case (checked), but sentence-final 'Appendix A.' or 'Section B.' is common, and a highlight on that ID covers two sentences.
suggested_fix: Treat 'X.' as an initial only when the original token is a capital, the previous token is a capitalised name-like word that is not a label word (Appendix, Section, Table, Figure, Part, Model, Type, Step...), and the next token is also capitalised name-like. Otherwise allow the boundary.
verifier: is_boundary (ingest.py:1484-1500) lowercases the token and then treats any non-math single letter followed by '.' as an initial. I imported the real split_sentences and fed it synthetic tokens. 'Proofs are given in Appendix A. We then train the model.', 'We call this variant model B. It uses fewer layers.' and 'See Section B. The second part follows.' each stay one sentence. 'Results are in Table 3. No other model comes close.' splits correctly. This is not in the build report's known limitations (that report only mentions the Figure 2 caption '(right)' case). It is a minor splitting error and does not affect the demo: low.

title: The fraction 1/√dk creates a stray one-character sentence ('1') and inverts the meaning of key sentences in Section 3.2.1
evidence: The build report says only that 1/√dk is read as '√dk 1'. The actual effect on demo doc.json is larger. p4.s16 = 'To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by √dk.' is followed by p4.s17 = '1' (a whole sentence ID, rect [446.27,605.44,450.24,615.4]). p4.s11 = '...except for the scaling factor of √dk.' is followed by p4.s12 = '1 Additive attention computes ...'. The numerator lands after 'dk.', is_boundary breaks there because '1' is not lowercase, and the numerator either becomes its own sentence or starts the next one. The text an LLM tour writer gets from outline.py therefore says to scale by √dk instead of dividing by it. My char-multiset audit of pages 1-10 (.../L2/audit_sent.py) found only these sentences and the known U+FFFD footnote p4.s22 to differ from the PDF.
suggested_fix: When building a Row, detect stacked words: a word that x-overlaps its neighbour and sits entirely above the row's core band is a numerator. Order it before the denominator and join the two as '1/√dk'. At minimum, do not break a sentence before a token that is stacked over the preceding token.
verifier: The demo doc.json shows the claimed text. p4.s16 = 'To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by √dk.' p4.s17 = '1', with rect [446.27,605.44,450.24,615.4], which lies inside s16's rect on the same line. p4.s11 ends '...scaling factor of √dk.' and p4.s12 = '1 Additive attention computes ...'. p4.s12's first rect starts at x=125.6, which overlaps s11's rect that ends at x=138.81 on that line. The garbling '√dk 1' is already a listed known limitation. The extra effects, a stray one-character sentence ID and the misplaced sentence boundary, are real but follow from it. The demo tour only highlights p4.s16, and its narration is hand-written and correct, so the visible impact is small: low.

title: Roman-numeral tables (IEEE 'TABLE IV') get IDs but never get referenced_by
evidence: CAPTION_RE (ingest.py:39) accepts `[IVX]+`, so 'TABLE IV: ...' becomes tabIV. FIG_REF_RE (43-45), however, only matches `\d+`. Calling the real link_references with the sentence 'Results are summarized in Table IV and Fig. 3.' gives [('table','IV',[]), ('figure','3',['p3.s1'])]: the table citation is dropped, so outline.py shows 'referenced_by: -' for every table in an IEEE-style paper.
suggested_fix: Extend the number group in FIG_REF_RE to `(?:\d+[a-z]?|[IVX]+\b)` (and the same in the list continuation), and keep _expand_numbers' range expansion limited to digits.
verifier: I called the real link_references with the sentence 'Results are summarized in Table IV and Fig. 3.'. It returns [('table','IV',[]), ('figure','3',['p3.s1'])]. FIG_REF_RE matches only 'Fig. 3', because its number group is \d+ while CAPTION_RE accepts [IVX]+. The reach is narrower than stated: the typical IEEE caption is 'TABLE IV' with no ':' or '.' after the numeral, and CAPTION_RE requires one, so many IEEE tables never get an ID at all. The finding applies only to 'Table IV:' / 'Table IV.' styles. That is a small gap in metadata: low.

title: Changing the speed mid-step has no audible effect until the next step, including on the step's later speech chunks
evidence:
Test: sh <scratch> rate_midstep.test.ts. It plays the demo 'abstract' step and calls engine.setRate(1.5) 1 s in, which is what App.tsx:120 does when the Speed select changes.

Utterances logged:
- "-1000ms rate 1 'The starting point...'"
- "5020ms rate 1 'The proposal is the Transforme...'" (the same step's second chunk, still at the old rate)

title: Spotlight mask uses evenodd, so where two spotlight holes overlap the overlap is dimmed
evidence:
PageView.tsx:169-175 draws one path: the page rect plus every hole as a rounded rect, filled with fillRule="evenodd". Overlapping holes cancel each other.
Test: t8.mjs built the same path in Chromium for a hole on fig2 and a hole on fig2.a (both padded by SPOT_PAD, radius 7) and called isPointInFill (true means dimmed): {"outside_both":true,"in_fig_only":false,"in_panel_and_fig":true}.

The demo tour never has two spotlights active at once.
suggested_fix: Render the dimming through an SVG <mask>: a white full-page rect plus black rounded-rect holes, applied to a full-page rect with the spotlight fill. Overlapping holes then form a union. Alternatively, merge overlapping hole rects before building the path.
verifier: PageView.tsx:169-175 draws the page rect plus every hole as one path with fillRule evenodd. title: Device-pixel-ratio changes are not observed: canvases keep the old resolution until the camera next moves
evidence:
Stage.tsx:45 and :70 read window.devicePixelRatio only inside planScales and planDetails, which run only on camera notifications or ResizeObserver callbacks. Nothing listens with matchMedia('(resolution: …dppx)') (grep finds only the prefers-reduced-motion query).

The page-4 canvases stayed at 3600x4659 for the base and 3232x2272 at 8 px/pt for the detail in all three states. At DPR 3 the view needs 12 px/pt and stays soft. title: figure-3 narration doesn't make sense when spoken: "Many heads reach the distant words more difficult."
evidence: tour.json line 353, step "figure-3", say: "...for the word making only, one color per head. Many heads reach the distant words more difficult." title: The box-label rule (always 6px above, left-aligned) blocks labels on 25 of the tour's 37 boxes; flipping below or inside does not fix it, a canvas ink test with 8 candidate positions does
evidence:
ScreenLayer.tsx:24-35 places each label at left=clamp(r.left,10,vp.width-120) and top=r.top-6 (translateY(-100%)), or inside at r.top+6 when r.top<=34. It never checks what is underneath.
Method: I bundled the player's own engine, cameraView, buildScene and project (sim.ts, esbuild from player/node_modules) to get every box's screen rect at its step's final view. labels.py and labels2.py then measure ink (fraction of pixels darker than 160 in a PyMuPDF render of paper.pdf) under an 80x21 px label, plus overlap with other boxes' strokes.
Result: of the 37 boxes the demo tour draws, the current rule lands on ink or another box's stroke for 25. This holds at both 1152x720 and 1112x767; only the 4 boxes the tour author picked for labels are clear.
Alternatives tested: trying above, then below, then inside still leaves 21 of 37 blocked, because in tables and diagrams the space below is as dense as the space above. Trying above-left, above-right, below-left, below-right, outside-left, outside-right, inside-top-left and inside-top-right, and taking the first clear one, leaves only 6 of 37 blocked (the dense Figure 1 sub-boxes in steps 6-9 and one Figure 3 box).
Why the canvas: doc.json alone cannot drive this, because Figure 1's arrows and boxes have no text layer. The rendered page canvas does show them.
Scripts: <scratch> and labels2.py.
suggested_fix: Choose the label position when it appears and again when the camera settles, not every frame. Convert each candidate screen rect to page points, read that small area from the page's base canvas with getImageData (the canvas is same-origin and only a few thousand pixels per candidate, at most 8 reads), and reject a candidate if more than about 1% of its pixels are dark, if it crosses another active box's stroke or label, or if it leaves the viewport. Keep the chosen side while the camera animates, and fall back to the current rule when the canvas is not rendered yet. Optionally add doc.json sentence and figure_text/table_text rects as a cheap pre-filter.
verifier: The cited code is described correctly: ScreenLayer.tsx:26-31 always places the label 6px above (or inside when r.top<=34) and checks nothing underneath. But this is a known limitation the build report lists explicitly (tour report): 'Contract limitation: box labels always sit 6px above a box, so in dense tables and diagrams they cover the row or element above. I worked around it by using labels only where the space above is empty (Encoder, Decoder, the Figure 4 top panel, Equation 1).' The headline '25 of 37 boxes blocked' is hypothetical. Counting tour.json, only 4 of the 37 boxes have a label (steps 6, 6, 14 and 33), and the reviewer agrees those 4 are clear. The other 33 boxes show no label, so no label in the demo actually collides. What remains is an enhancement proposal (a canvas ink-test placement) for a documented contract limitation, not a new defect.
